title: Gaza's children: the walk to school

scenes.say: In Gaza, children have gone back to school.
And they are being killed on the way there.
scenes.text: Killed on the way | to school

scenes.say: This is what a ceasefire looks like for Gaza's children.
scenes.title: Gaza's walk to school

scenes.say: The academic year resumed on 19 September, after nearly three years of disruption from the war.
scenes.title: A school year, at last
scenes.speak: The academic year resumed on the nineteenth of September, after nearly three years of disruption from the war.

scenes.say: But the strikes and sniper fire did not stop.
Mohammed Hamad was 14, an eighth-grader near the top of his class.
scenes.text: Mohammed Hamad, 14: | near the top of his class

scenes.say: On 17 October, he walked home from school in Deir el-Balah with his 10-year-old brother, Abdullah.
scenes.speak: On the seventeenth of October, he walked home from school in Deir el-Balah with his ten-year-old brother, Abdullah.

scenes.say: An Israeli strike hit the road. Mohammed was killed. Abdullah survived.
His father, Riyad, now lives in a tent in Deir el-Balah.
scenes.text: "He was not just my son, he was my friend."

scenes.say: Abdullah is now afraid to go to school alone.
Between 18 and 24 October, 10 children and a teacher were killed.
scenes.label: Children aged 6 to 16 killed, 18–24 October, plus a teacher (Gaza Ministry of Education)
scenes.speak: Between the eighteenth and the twenty-fourth of October, ten children and a teacher were killed.

scenes.say: Two girls were wounded at morning assembly. Five students were hurt at a university.
scenes.title: At school, not just on the road
items: Muradiya School, Jabalia: 2 girls wounded at assembly
Islamic University, Gaza City: 5 students injured

scenes.say: Since the ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,574 Palestinians in Gaza.
scenes.label: Killed since the October 2025 ceasefire, Gaza Ministry of Health
scenes.speak: Since the ceasefire, Israel has killed at least one thousand five hundred and seventy-four Palestinians in Gaza.

scenes.say: The danger is greatest near the Yellow Line.
Under the ceasefire, Israel controlled 53 per cent of Gaza. The UN says it now controls more than 65.
scenes.speak: Under the ceasefire, Israel controlled fifty-three per cent of Gaza. The U N says it now controls more than sixty-five.

scenes.say: As the line moves west, more homes and tent schools come within range.
scenes.text: The line moves west. | Schools come within range.

scenes.say: At least 66 children have been killed close to the line.
scenes.label: Children killed near the Yellow Line
scenes.speak: At least sixty-six children have been killed close to the line.

scenes.say: On 21 October, Suad Abd Rabbo, a fourth-grader, set off for school with her bag and books.
scenes.speak: On the twenty-first of October, Suad Abd Rabbo, a fourth-grader, set off for school with her bag and books.
scenes.text: 21 October: | Suad Abd Rabbo, fourth grade

scenes.say: Soon after, her sister ran home shouting that Suad had been shot.
Her mother, Aliaa, remembers.
scenes.text: "I ran out barefoot. She was bleeding, crying and screaming."

scenes.say: For families, every morning is now a choice between school and safety.
Riyad Hamad again.
scenes.text: "The child is supposed to bury his father, not the father bury his child."

scenes.say: A ceasefire is measured by whether children come home from school.
In Gaza, too many don't.
